proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(r_n=a_n/2\), and let \(\kappa_0\) be the constant in \(\text{lem:finite-legal-probe}\).  Define
\[
 \mathcal A_n=\left\{
 \|\widehat p_n-p_n\|_\infty\le\kappa_0r_n
 \right\}.
\tag{15}
\]
For a single multinomial coordinate, the exponential Markov argument applied to a bounded Bernoulli summand gives
\(P_n(|\widehat p_{nj}-p_{nj}|>t)\le2e^{-2nt^2}\).  A union bound therefore yields
\[
 \sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M}P_n(\mathcal A_n^c)
 \le2|\mathcal J|\exp\{-2n\kappa_0^2r_n^2\}=o(1),
\tag{16}
\]
because \(\sqrt n a_n\to\infty\).

On \(\mathcal A_n\), every \(b\in\mathcal B(p_n,r_n)\) satisfies
\[
 \|b-\widehat p_n\|_\infty
 \le r_n+\kappa_0r_n<a_n.
\tag{17}
\]
It is legal by definition, so \(\mathcal B(p_n,r_n)\subseteq B_n\).  Consequently
\[
 T_n(g)\ge E_{p_n,r_n}(g)\ge V_{p_n,r_n}(g)
 \quad\text{for every }g,
\tag{18}
\]
where the second inequality is \((\mathrm{P1})\).  Conditional monotonicity of lower quantiles gives
\[
 c_n\ge Q_{1-\alpha}
 \{V_{p_n,r_n}(G^*)\mid\widehat p_n\}
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal A_n.
\tag{19}
\]

We prove that the critical value on the right calibrates the finite probe maximum uniformly, including when its scale vanishes.  Suppress the indices \((p_n,r_n)\), write the probe rows as \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\), where \(m\le N_0\), and put
\[
 H_n=\sqrt n(\widehat p_n-p_n),\quad
 V(g)=\max_{\nu\le m}|a_\nu^{\mathsf T}g|,\quad
 A=A_{p_n,r_n},\quad s=s_{p_n,r_n}.
\]
Subtracting a constant from a row does not change its value on a vector whose coordinates sum to zero.  We may therefore center every row so that \(\|a_\nu\|_\infty\le2A\).  If \(A=0\), \((\mathrm{P2})\)--\((\mathrm{P3})\) show on \(\mathcal A_n\) that
\[
 \Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(\widehat p_n)=\Phi(p_n)
\tag{20}
\]
exactly.  Hence only \(A>0\) remains.  In that case \((\mathrm{P3})\) gives
\[
 \frac{A}{\sqrt n,s}\le\frac{1}{c_0\sqrt n,r_n}=o(1).
\tag{21}
\]

Let \(G_p\sim N\{0,\Sigma(p_n)\}\).  We first compare \(V(H_n)\) with \(V(G_p)\).  For clarity, the fixed-dimensional replacement bound is derived here.  If
\(X_i=(a_\nu^{\mathsf T}(e_{O_{ni}}-p_n))_{\nu\le m}\), then
\[
 \max_\nu|X_{i\nu}|\le4A,
 \qquad
 \sum_{\nu=1}^m\mathbb E X_{i\nu}^2\le ms^2,
\tag{22}
\]
and \(n^{-1/2}\sum_iX_i=(a_\nu^{\mathsf T}H_n)_\nu\).  Convolve the indicator of the cube \([-t,t]^m\) with a smooth mollifier of radius \(\eta\).  The sums of absolute derivatives of orders one, two, and three of the resulting function are bounded by \(C_m\eta^{-1}\), \(C_m\eta^{-2}\), and \(C_m\eta^{-3}\), respectively.  Replace the \(X_i/\sqrt n\)'s one at a time by independent Gaussian vectors with the same covariance.  The constant, linear, and quadratic Taylor terms cancel.  By \((22)\),
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb E\|X_i/\sqrt n\|_\infty^3
 \le \frac{4Am s^2}{\sqrt n},
\]
and the matching Gaussian terms obey the same bound up to a constant depending only on \(m\).  Taylor's formula with integral remainder therefore gives
\[
 \left|\mathbb E f_{t,\eta}\{(a_\nu^{\mathsf T}H_n)_\nu\}
 -\mathbb E f_{t,\eta}\{(a_\nu^{\mathsf T}G_p)_\nu\}\right|
 \le \frac{C_mAs^2}{\sqrt n\,\eta^3}.
\tag{23}
\]

Apply \(\text{lem:scale-free-unsigned-gaussian-max}\) to the at most \(m\) Gaussian coordinates, padding with duplicate zero coordinates if \(m<3\).  Its largest standard deviation is \(s\), and hence
\[
 \sup_{t\ge0}P\{|V(G_p)-t|\le\eta\}
 \le C_m\eta/s.
\tag{24}
\]
Take \(\eta=s\delta_n\), where
\[
 \delta_n=\left(\frac{A}{\sqrt n,s}\right)^{1/4}.
\]
Equations \((21)\)--\((24)\), together with the two mollifier inclusions, imply
\[
 \sup_t\left|P_n\{V(H_n)\le t\}-P\{V(G_p)\le t\}\right|
 \le C_m(\delta_n+\delta_n^{-3}A/\sqrt n s)=o(1)
\tag{25}
\]
uniformly over \(P_n\in\mathcal M\).  This is a relative, rather than additive, Gaussian approximation; it remains valid for \(s\downarrow0\) because \((21)\) uses \(\sqrt n r_n\to\infty\).

It remains to replace the population covariance by the conditional plug-in covariance.  For a probability vector \(q\) and a standard Gaussian vector \(W\), define
\[
 \widetilde G_j(q)=\sqrt{q_j}W_j-q_j\sum_k\sqrt{q_k}W_k.
\tag{26}
\]
Then \(\widetilde G(q)\) has covariance \(\Sigma(q)\).  The coefficient matrix in \((26)\) is Lipschitz in \((\sqrt{q_j})_j\) on the unit sphere, so
\[
 \mathbb E_W\|\widetilde G(\widehat p_n)-\widetilde G(p_n)\|_2^2
 \le C_{|\mathcal J|}\|\sqrt{\widehat p_n}-\sqrt{p_n}\|_2^2.
\tag{27}
\]
For \(p_{nj}>0\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_n}(\sqrt{\widehat p_{nj}}-\sqrt{p_{nj}})^2
 \le\frac{\mathbb E_{P_n}(\widehat p_{nj}-p_{nj})^2}{p_{nj}}
 =\frac{1-p_{nj}}n,
\tag{28}
\]
while a zero population atom has zero empirical count almost surely.  Summing \((28)\) and using \((27)\) gives
\[
 \max_{\nu\le m}|a_\nu^{\mathsf T}\{
 \widetilde G(\widehat p_n)-\widetilde G(p_n)\}|
 =O_{P_n\times P^*}(A/\sqrt n)=o_{P_n\times P^*}(s),
\tag{29}
\]
uniformly, by \((21)\).  The principal-square-root draw \(G^*\) has the same conditional law as \(\widetilde G(\widehat p_n)\).  Combining \((24)\) and \((29)\) transfers the entire conditional distribution, and therefore its lower \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile, at relative error \(o_P(s)\).  More explicitly, if \(q_n^*\) is that conditional quantile, then \((24)\), \((25)\), and the defining inequality
\(P^*\{V(G^*)\le q_n^*\}\ge1-\alpha\) yield
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M}
 P_n\{V(H_n)>q_n^*\}\le\alpha.
\tag{30}
\]
The lower-quantile convention causes no problem.  When \(s>0\), \(V(G_p)\) dominates the absolute value of a centered Gaussian with variance \(s^2\), so its \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile is positive; \((24)\) makes its distribution continuous there.  When \(s=0\), \((\mathrm{P3})\) forces the exact-flat branch \((20)\).

Finally, on \(\mathcal A_n\) the sample support is contained in the population support almost surely.  If neither fallback branch occurs, \((\mathrm{P2})\), \((19)\), and \((30)\) give
\[
 \begin{split}
 P_n\{\Phi(p_n)\notin C_n,\mathcal A_n\}
 &\le P_n\{\sqrt n\|\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(\widehat p_n)-\Phi(p_n)\|_\infty>c_n,\mathcal A_n\}\\
 &\le P_n\{V(H_n)>q_n^*\}\le\alpha+o(1)
 \end{split}
\tag{31}
\]
uniformly.  If \(B_n=\varnothing\) or \(M(\widehat p_n)=0\), the definition sets \(C_n=\mathbb R^2\), so noncoverage is impossible on that branch.  Adding \((16)\) to \((31)\) proves
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P_n\in\mathcal M}
 P_n\{\Phi(p_n)\in C_n\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
The result concerns the observed-law sharp endpoint vector.  By the imported identification theorem, the causal identified set is \(\Theta_I(p_n)=[L(p_n),U(p_n)]\); the proof does not define the causal target as the plug-in or Gaussian functional.

added_lemmas.statement:
There are constants \(r_0>0\), \(\kappa_0\in(0,1/4)\), \(c_0>0\), and \(N_0<\infty\), depending only on \(K\), \(\lvert\mathcal X\rvert\), \(\epsilon\), and \(m_*\), with the following property.  For every \(p\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfying \(M(p)\ge m_*\) and every \(0<r\le r_0\), one can choose at most \(N_0\) triples \((b_{\nu,+},b_{\nu,-},a_\nu)\), where \(b_{\nu,+},b_{\nu,-}\in\mathcal B(p,r)\), every instrument cell of both bases is positive, and \(a_\nu\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}\), such that
\[
 |a_\nu^{\mathsf T}g|
 \le\max_{\varsigma\in\{+,-\}}\|d_{b_{\nu,\varsigma}}(g)\|_\infty,
 \qquad g\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}.
\]
Writing
\[
 V_{p,r}(g)=\max_{\nu}|a_\nu^{\mathsf T}g|,
 \qquad
 A_{p,r}=\max_\nu\inf_{c\in\mathbb R}
       \|a_\nu-c\mathbf 1\|_\infty,
 \qquad
 s_{p,r}=\max_\nu\{a_\nu^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(p)a_\nu\}^{1/2},
\]
the following statements hold.
\[
 V_{p,r}(g)\le E_{p,r}(g)\quad\text{for every }g,
\tag{P1}
\]
and, for every \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal J)\) with \(\operatorname{supp}(q)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(p)\), \(\|q-p\|_\infty\le\kappa_0r\), and \(M(q)>0\),
\[
 \|\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(q)-\Phi(p)\|_\infty
 \le V_{p,r}(q-p).
\tag{P2}
\]
Moreover, either \(A_{p,r}=0\), in which case the left side of \((\mathrm{P2})\) is zero for every such \(q\), or
\[
 s_{p,r}\ge c_0rA_{p,r}.
\tag{P3}
\]
Thus every form used in \(V_{p,r}\) is the derivative at a positive-cell legal law; no value of \(d_b\) outside \(\mathcal D_b\) at a zero-cell base is used.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We give the finite construction.  It is useful first to write the legal model in coordinates in which legality is preserved visibly.

\paragraph{1. Latent response-type coordinates.}
For \(x\in\mathcal X\), let \(\mathcal T_x\) be the finite set of tuples
\[
 t=(d_0,d_1,s_0,s_1,y_0,y_1)
 \in\{0,1\}^4\times\mathcal Y^2
\]
such that \(d_0\le d_1\), and such that
\(\rho(x)(s_1-s_0)\ge0\) whenever \(d_0<d_1\).  Put
\(\mu_{xt}=Q(X=x,T=t)\) and
\(e_x=Q(Z=1\mid X=x)\), choosing any \(e_x\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\) when \(Q(X=x)=0\).  Conditional instrument independence and the three consistency assumptions give the observed-law formula
\[
 p_{xz,a}=e_x^z(1-e_x)^{1-z}
 \sum_{t\in\mathcal T_x}\mu_{xt}
 \mathbf 1\{A_z(t)=a\},
\tag{1}
\]
where
\[
 A_z(t)=\bigl(d_z,s_{d_z},s_{d_z}y_{d_z}\bigr).
\]
Conversely, nonnegative \(\mu_{xt}\) summing to one, together with propensities in \([\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), define through \((1)\) a full law satisfying conditional instrument independence, consistency, no defiers, and the declared cellwise selection monotonicity.  This is a direct finite disintegration: draw \((X,T)\) with masses \(\mu\), draw \(Z\) conditionally Bernoulli with parameter \(e_X\) independently of \(T\), and then apply \(A_Z(T)\).

Let
\[
 \mathcal S_x=\{t\in\mathcal T_x:d_0=0,d_1=1, s_0=s_1=1\}.
\]
For \(t\in\mathcal S_x\), only the pair \((y_0,y_1)\) varies.  The imported endpoint representation and the capacity definition give
\[
 M(p)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\sum_{t\in\mathcal S_x}\mu_{xt}.
\tag{2}
\]
There are \(R=\lvert\mathcal X\rvert K^2\) terms in \((2)\).  Hence \(M(p)\ge m_*\) supplies a donor \(\omega=(x_\omega,t_\omega)\) with
\[
 \mu_\omega\ge \underline\mu:=m_*/R.
\tag{3}
\]

For \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \((i,j)\in\mathcal Y^2\), denote by \(t_{xij}\) the survivor-complier type with outcomes \((i,j)\).  If \(u=(u_{xij})\) is nonnegative and sums to one, the transfer
\[
 \mu^{u,\delta}=\mu-\delta e_\omega
       +\delta\sum_{x,i,j}u_{xij}e_{x,t_{xij}},
 \qquad 0<\delta\le\underline\mu/2,
\tag{4}
\]
is nonnegative and normalized.  Every added type has \(s_0=s_1=1\), so it satisfies either sign of selection monotonicity.  Both the removed and added mass in \((4)\) is survivor-complier mass; consequently \((2)\), conditional instrument independence, no defiers, and selection monotonicity are all preserved.  Keeping the \(e_x\)'s fixed (and taking \(e_x=1/2\) in a formerly empty covariate cell) preserves overlap.  Formula \((1)\) also shows
\[
 \|p^{u,\delta}-p\|_\infty\le\delta.
\tag{5}
\]
In capacity coordinates the same substitution is exact:
\[
 H_x(p^{u,\delta})-H_x(p)
 =\delta\sum_{i,j}u_{xij}(e_i^L+e_j^U)
 -\mathbf 1\{x=x_\omega\}\delta(e_{y_0(\omega)}^L+e_{y_1(\omega)}^U).
\tag{6}
\]
Here \(e_i^L\) and \(e_j^U\) are the standard basis vectors in the lower and upper \(K\)-blocks.  Identity \((6)\) follows by inserting \((1)\) in the two conditional contrasts defining \(H_x\): under \(Z=0\) the added complier is observed in \((D,S,SY)=(0,1,i)\), under \(Z=1\) it is observed in \((1,1,j)\), and multiplication by \(q_x\) cancels the conditional normalization.

The only additional face coordinate is the sign of the selected-complier total difference.  For \(\rho(x)=1\), the legal type with \((s_0,s_1)=(0,1)\) moves only the upper total; for \(\rho(x)=-1\), the legal type with \((s_0,s_1)=(1,0)\) moves only the lower total.  Such a transfer can be paired with \((4)\).  If spending survivor mass would cross the floor in \((2)\), then \(M(p)-m_*<\underline\mu/4\), while the nonsurvivor mass is at least \(1-m_*\); one of its finitely many response types therefore has mass at least \((1-m_*)/\sum_x|\mathcal T_x|\), and an equal transfer from that type to a survivor type restores \((2)\).  If the nonsurvivor mass is smaller than this fixed amount, then \(M(p)-m_*\) is bounded below by a fixed amount and the first transfer itself stays above the floor for all \(r\le r_0\).  This two-case construction supplies both one-sided total faces without adding an assumption.

\paragraph{2. Finite face legalization.}
There are finitely many sign patterns for the coordinates of \(H_x\), finitely many choices of the smaller survivor total, and finitely many active threshold cuts in \(F_L\) and \(F_U\).  Call a joint choice a face \(F\).  On the relative interior of \(F\), the three capacity maps are linear:
\[
 \bar N_e=c_e^F H,
 \qquad \bar M=c_M^F H,
 \qquad e\in\{L,U\},
\tag{7}
\]
where the entries of \(c_e^F,c_M^F\) belong to \(\{-1,0,1\}\).  At a tie, every one-sided branch is one of these same finitely many rows.  If \(b\) has positive instrument cells and lies in the relative interior of \(F\), the quotient rule gives the linear face form
\[
 \ell_{F,b,e}(g)=
 \frac{\{c_e^F-\Phi_e(b)c_M^F\}\,D H_b[g]}{M(b)}.
\tag{8}
\]

We next verify that the transfers above legalize all rows needed on an ambient empirical segment.  For an active lower coordinate, put
\(A=b_{x0,(0,1,k)}\), \(B=b_{x1,(0,1,k)}\),
\(q_z=q_{xz}(b)\), and \(R=A/q_0-B/q_1\).  Direct differentiation gives
\[
 D H_{x,Lk,b}[g]
 =\mathbf 1_F\left[g_xR+b_x\left\{
 \frac{g_A}{q_0}-\frac{A g_{q_0}}{q_0^2}
 -\frac{g_B}{q_1}+\frac{B g_{q_1}}{q_1^2}
 \right\}\right],
\tag{9}
\]
and the upper block has the same formula with the two instrument arms and treatment labels interchanged.  The symbol \(\mathbf 1_F\) means that the displayed sign branch belongs to \(F\); at equality the two values \(0\) and the bracketed row are both included in the finite face list.  Overlap gives
\(q_z\ge\epsilon b_x\) at every positive legal base.  Thus all denominators in \((9)\) are positive.

For completeness, the finite algebraic certificate is as follows.  Order the coordinates in \((9)\) as
\[
 (g_A,g_B,g_{q_0},g_{q_1},g_x).
\]
Changing the mass of \(t_{xij}\) changes exactly one lower selected numerator and one upper selected numerator, as shown in \((6)\).  Changing a protected-complier type changes exactly one of the two survivor totals.  Changing \(e_x\) changes \((q_0,q_1)\) in the direction \((-b_x,b_x)\).  Therefore, after constants are quotiented out, the matrix whose columns are these transfer effects is triangular when the coordinates are ordered as selected numerators, survivor totals, and propensity; its diagonal is
\[
 \left(\frac{b_x}{q_0},\frac{b_x}{q_1},1,\ldots,1\right).
\tag{10}
\]
Every nonzero diagonal entry in \((10)\) lies in \([1,\epsilon^{-1}]\).  Hence the transfer columns span every coefficient change appearing in \((9)\), with a right inverse bounded solely by \(K\), \(\lvert\mathcal X\rvert\), and \(\epsilon\).  Equation \((6)\) shows that the required columns are realized by legal response-type transfers, including when the target covariate cell was empty.  The preceding paired transfer handles the survivor-total column while respecting \(M\ge m_*\).  This is the promised symbolic legal-law realization; it uses no derivative at an empty-cell base.

Choose \(\delta=\beta r\), where \(\beta>0\) is smaller than the reciprocal of twice the finite right-inverse bound and also ensures \(\delta\le\underline\mu/2\).  For every face \(F\), take all vertices of the transfer box generated by \((4)\), the protected-type transfers, and inward propensity moves of size at most \(\delta\).  If a propensity equals \(\epsilon\) or \(1-\epsilon\), only the legal inward vertex is used; the missing outward coefficient is dominated by the corresponding selected-numerator vertex furnished by the same column of the right inverse in \((10)\).  Take \(\kappa_0\) smaller than \(\beta\) divided by four times that right-inverse bound.  Substitution in \((9)\), followed by multiplication by the finite rows in \((7)\), then gives the following coefficient inclusion for every \(q=p+h\) with \(\|h\|_\infty\le\kappa_0r\): every operative face row on the segment \(p+th\), \(0\le t\le1\), belongs to
\[
 \operatorname{conv}\{a_\nu:\nu\in I_F\}
 \quad\text{modulo }\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}.
\tag{11}
\]
To see the inequality at a boundary rather than merely its first-order version, clear the positive factors \(q_0q_1M\) in \((8)\)--\((9)\).  Each remaining coefficient is separately affine in the selected numerators, \(q_0^{-1}\), \(q_1^{-1}\), and \(M^{-1}\).  A scalar lying between two endpoint values is their convex combination; applying this identity successively to these finitely many coordinates expresses the row as a convex combination of the transfer-box vertices.  If an ambient coordinate is at most \(\kappa_0r\) beyond a one-sided legal endpoint, the right-inverse column in \((10)\) supplies a legal vertex at distance \(\beta r\) on the selected-numerator coordinate, and the choice of \(\kappa_0\) puts the extrapolated value between the resulting two coefficient values.  This proves \((11)\) exactly, not up to a Taylor remainder.  The min, max, and positive-part inequalities cause no loss: on each open segment they merely select one row from \((7)\), and at a crossing their one-sided slopes are the adjacent listed rows.

Before taking the vertices, seed every formerly empty covariate cell with survivor mass \(\beta_0r\), where \(\beta_0>0\) is smaller than \(\beta\) divided by four times the number of cells.  Formula \((6)\) shows that this keeps the base legal and positive in both instrument arms; the remaining transfer box is recentered after the seeding, so the coefficient inclusion \((11)\) is unchanged.  Every resulting vertex base is legal, is within distance \(r\) of \(p\), and has \(M\ge m_*\).

For an ordinary feasible face, use the two opposite transfer-box vertices bracketing its coefficient row.  At a one-sided legal boundary, use the boundary vertex and the selected-numerator vertex supplied by the same right-inverse column in \((10)\).  The scalar identity used in proving \((11)\), now applied to both signs of the endpoint row and to every vertex of the finite box, gives a row \(a_\nu\) and two legal positive-cell bases \(b_{\nu,+},b_{\nu,-}\) satisfying
\[
 |a_\nu^{\mathsf T}g|
 \le\max_{\varsigma\in\{+,-\}}\|d_{b_{\nu,\varsigma}}(g)\|_\infty
 \le E_{p,r}(g).
\]
The one-sided case is exact because the unavailable branch is zero while the compensating selected-numerator vertex has the opposite signed row; the positive part is therefore bounded by the maximum of the two displayed absolute derivatives.  There are only finitely many faces, columns, signs, and box vertices, so their number is bounded by \(N_0\).  This proves \((\mathrm{P1})\).

The segment \(t\mapsto p+t(q-p)\) crosses only finitely many of the faces in \((7)\).  On every open piece, \((11)\) and the fundamental theorem of calculus give, for each endpoint,
\[
 \begin{split}
 |\Phi_e(q)-\Phi_e(p)|
 &=\left|\int_0^1 \dot\Phi_e\{p+t(q-p)\}\,dt\right|\\
 &\le\int_0^1\max_\nu|a_\nu^{\mathsf T}(q-p)|\,dt
 =V_{p,r}(q-p).
 \end{split}
\tag{12}
\]
The aggregate denominator stays positive on the segment after reducing \(r_0\): the same cleared-denominator calculation bounds its change by a fixed multiple of \(\|q-p\|_\infty\), while \(M(p)\ge m_*\).  Formula \((12)\) proves \((\mathrm{P2})\).

\paragraph{3. Relative traction or exact flatness.}
For a vector \(a\), multinomial variance has the identity
\[
 a^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(p)a
 =\frac12\sum_{j,k\in\mathcal J}p_jp_k(a_j-a_k)^2.
\tag{13}
\]
The two observed realizations of the donor \(\omega\) in \((3)\) have probabilities at least \(\epsilon\underline\mu\).  The right-inverse identity \((10)\) and the transfer size \(\delta=\beta r\) imply that, unless every probe row is constant, some probe row \(a_\nu\) has, between these donor realizations (or between one of them and a donor atom in the same instrument cell), coefficient difference at least
\[
 c_1r\max_\nu\inf_c\|a_\nu-c\mathbf1\|_\infty
 =c_1rA_{p,r},
\tag{14}
\]
where \(c_1>0\) depends only on the finite right inverse, \(\epsilon\), and \(m_*\).  This is the score version of survivor padding: if a face row distinguishes any latent selected outcome, moving \(\delta\) mass from the positive donor to that outcome changes the coefficient of a donor-supported observed atom by \(\delta\) times that distinction.  If it distinguishes only an instrument denominator, the propensity column in \((10)\) gives the same conclusion.  These exhaust the five coordinate kinds in \((9)\).

Combining \((13)\), \((14)\), and \((3)\) yields
\[
 s_{p,r}\ge \epsilon\underline\mu\,c_1rA_{p,r}=c_0rA_{p,r},
\]
after decreasing \(c_0\) if necessary.  If \(A_{p,r}=0\), every \(a_\nu\) is constant, so \(a_\nu^{\mathsf T}(q-p)=0\) because both probability vectors sum to one.  Then \((12)\) makes the endpoint increment exactly zero.  This proves \((\mathrm{P3})\) and the local-flatness branch.
added_lemmas.justification: The lemma replaces the informal legal-realization handle by finitely many positive-cell latent-simplex probes and supplies the scale dichotomy needed for relative calibration.
added_lemmas.gap: Capacity-space face enumeration alone does not imply that the same rows occur at nearby observed laws satisfying the causal restrictions, and an additive Gaussian approximation is inadequate when every endpoint variance vanishes.
added_lemmas.consumer: The uniform-coverage theorem uses the exact pathwise domination and the lower bound on probe scale; the zero-scale branch supplies exact local flatness.

source.locator: Proposition 4 (Uniform density bounds for unsigned maxima), arXiv:2605.29066v2, Section 2.2
source.verbatim_statement: Let \(Z \sim N(0,\Sigma)\) be a centered Gaussian vector in \(\mathbb R^p\) with \(p \ge 3\), let \(\sigma_{\max}^2 = \max_{1 \le i \le p} \mathbb E[Z_i^2]\), and let \(M^* = \max_{1 \le i \le p} |Z_i|\). Then, for any \(t \ge 0\), \[\lim_{\delta \downarrow 0} \frac{1}{\delta} \mathbb P\left\{t \le M^* < t+\delta\right\} \le \frac{4\log(2p)}{\sigma_{\max} \vee t}.\]

attestation.note: Transcribed from the TeX source of arXiv:2605.29066v2, Proposition 4, lines carrying the label prop:unsigned-density-bound; notation was normalized to the present LaTeX style without changing the claim.

proposed.statement: For every deterministic sequence \(a_n\to0\) with \(\sqrt n a_n\to\infty\), the total common-Gaussian rectangle satisfies \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P_n\in\mathcal M}P_n\{\Phi(p_n)\in C_n\}\ge1-\alpha.\] The full-plane branch covers identically when \(B_n=\varnothing\) or \(M(\widehat p_n)=0\), and the infimum includes legal arrays with arbitrarily vanishing covariate cells, survivor cells, active-cut gaps, and endpoint variances.
proposed.justification: Uniform joint coverage is the headline result and cannot be replaced by endpoint-wise Bonferroni or pointwise bootstrap validity.
proposed.gap: Existing Gaussian and directional-bootstrap results do not legalize changing capacity faces in the observed causal-law image or provide relative calibration when the full endpoint scale collapses.
proposed.consumer: Clinical and labor applications using survivor-complier ordinal outcomes obtain one honest confidence statement for the entire sharp benefit interval.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The completed proof uses the finite legal-probe lemma and the cited scale-free anti-concentration result directly, so the dependency metadata must replace the former open-ended handle by those established premises.

prose_updates.tldr: The accepted sharp-identification theorem supplies \(\Theta_I(p)=[L(p),U(p)]\) for the survivor-complier probability of benefit. The present result proves that the explicit nearby-legal-base envelope and its common-Gaussian max-norm rectangle cover the endpoint vector uniformly over every legal triangular array under only fixed instrument overlap and \(M(p)\ge m_*\), even when individual covariate or survivor cells, cut gaps, and both endpoint variances vanish. A finite latent-simplex probe construction turns every operative capacity face into a derivative at a positive-cell legal base. It yields either exact local flatness or probe standard deviation at least a constant times \(a_n\) times coefficient oscillation; this makes the multinomial and plug-in covariance errors relatively negligible because \(\sqrt n a_n\to\infty\). Separated regular faces retain exact oracle Gaussian calibration, while the established root-\(n\) width and \(K=4\) diagnostics remain unchanged.

project_justification.fill: The total legal-base envelope retains every nearby support and cut face and uses one Gaussian draw for both endpoints. Finite response-type transfers now prove the legal face lift, exact segment domination, and a flatness-or-traction dichotomy; scale-free anti-concentration then transfers the lower conditional critical value uniformly, including a collapsing endpoint scale.

prose_updates.related_work: The accepted CausalSmith survivor-complier benefit result supplies the exact sharp endpoint formula and full-law sharpness; identification is imported rather than reproved. Angrist, Imbens, and Rubin (1996) support conditional instrument randomization, treatment consistency, and no defiers, while Dong and Heiler (2026) support treatment-mediated selection and outcome consistency together with covariate-specific weak selection monotonicity. The fixed \(\epsilon\) overlap bound and fixed \(m_*\) denominator floor are uniform-class strengthenings here. Fang and Santos (2019) and Hong and Li (2018) explain derivative-resampling methods, but their generic results do not construct the required nearby legal observed laws. Frandsen and Pond (2025) begin from asymptotically normal bound estimators; Imai and Okamoto (2026) require supplied uniformly asymptotically linear endpoints and nonvanishing standard deviations; Andrews and Guggenberger (2009) work with standardized moment-inequality statistics of positive component variance. The finite latent-simplex legalization proved here is model-specific and distinct from those premises. Vijaykumar (2026), Proposition 4, supplies the scale-free density bound for the unsigned Gaussian maximum used after the probe traction inequality; it does not supply that legal geometry or the relative multinomial comparison.
prose_updates.interpretation: The rectangle is a simultaneous confidence set for the sharp endpoint pair \(\Phi(p_n)=(L(p_n),U(p_n))\), not a redefinition of the causal probability \(\theta_B\). Because the imported identification theorem gives \(\Theta_I(p_n)=[L(p_n),U(p_n)]\), covering both endpoints gives one honest inferential statement about the entire sharp benefit interval. The common draw preserves endpoint dependence and is generally narrower than coordinatewise Bonferroni calibration on regular faces.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The uniform proof is asymptotic and uses fixed finite \(K\) and \(\mathcal X\), fixed overlap \(\epsilon\), fixed aggregate floor \(m_*\), and \(\sqrt n a_n\to\infty\). It supplies no finite-sample coverage error constant and no polynomial-time claim for computing the legal-base supremum. Zero-cell algebraic derivatives remain total scaffolding only: the proof's load-bearing probe rows are all realized at positive-cell legal bases. If the aggregate empirical mass is zero or the random legal base set is empty, the stated full-plane fallback remains part of the procedure.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Sharp identification is imported from the accepted parent and is not a contribution of this note. The contribution is uniform joint inference for that fixed endpoint map under the inherited finite binary-instrument model, strengthened only by fixed instrument overlap and a fixed aggregate survivor-complier mass floor. No lower bound is imposed on an individual covariate cell, survivor cell, active-cut gap, or endpoint variance, and no support screen, variance floor, endpoint-wise Bonferroni device, or deterministic calibration guard is introduced. Exact oracle behavior is asserted separately only on fixed separated regular faces; the uniform theorem requires honesty, not exactness, on tied or degenerating faces.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem now closes the headline requirement: one common-Gaussian rectangle covers both sharp endpoints uniformly without individual support, gap, or variance lower bounds.
statement_notes.gap: The new finite legal-probe lemma supplies the model-specific observed-law lift absent from generic directional-bootstrap theory, and its variance-traction branch makes critical-value transfer relative rather than merely additive.
statement_notes.consumer: Applications with ordinal survivor-complier outcomes can report one honest confidence statement for the full sharp probability-of-benefit interval while retaining root-\(n\) width on the established emerging-support and tied-cut arrays.
